summary: Morpheus leads Neo down a long dark hall to a door and tells him only Neo can step through it. Neo hesitates, pulls back, and argues that he still doesn't believe, so there is no point. Morpheus asks what Neo believes in; Neo says his world was a lie and he believes in nothing. Morpheus reframes faith as something of the heart and gut, and reaffirms that Neo is the One. Neo challenges him about the five men before him; Morpheus admits he once wrongly believed he could anoint anyone and that it was 'all about me,' and that after the fifth he lost his way and doubted the Oracle and himself — until he saw Neo and his world changed. Morpheus asks only for Neo's trust. Neo feels the pull of Morpheus's certainty and agrees. As he reaches for the handle, it turns on its own and a woman in white opens the door, greeting him on time.

what_changes.before: Resisting and doubting, telling Morpheus 'I don't think this is a good idea' and that he will never believe, so 'what's the point?'
what_changes.after: Surrenders to Morpheus's intensity, agreeing to trust him despite not believing.
what_changes.evidence: Neo feels a rush from Morpheus's intensity, the unadulterated confidence of a zealot. NEO All right.

what_changes.before: Having believed he could anoint the One himself and that it was all about him, a belief that proved wrong over five failed men.
what_changes.after: Admits he misunderstood the Oracle and now believes Neo is the sixth and last, the One.
what_changes.evidence: I believed that all I had to do was point my finger and anoint whoever I chose. I was wrong, Neo. Terribly wrong.

what_changes.before: Physically recoiling from the door, 'His hand reaches but stops, hovering over the spherical handle. He backs away.'
what_changes.after: Moves to open the door and crosses the threshold of decision.
what_changes.evidence: He reaches for the handle which turns without him even touching it. A WOMAN wearing white opens the door.

event_hint.one_line: Morpheus persuades a doubting Neo to trust him and step through the Oracle's door.

minds.wants: To get Neo to cross the threshold of the Oracle's door — not by argument, but by transferring his own certainty onto Neo as trust.
minds.feels: A zealot's unshakable conviction, but one that has been tempered and almost broken by five prior failures. His certainty is real yet hard-won, and the memory of those five men is a live wound ('Not a day or night passes that I do not think of them').
minds.shows: Blazing-eyed, controlled, almost sermonizing intensity — the 'unadulterated confidence of a zealot.' He hides the pain the fifth-man question costs him ('tries to hide his heart being wrenched').
minds.basis: The stage direction that Morpheus 'tries to hide his heart being wrenched from his chest' when Neo raises the five men; his admission that he 'was wrong, terribly wrong' and 'lost my way'; the pivot from reason to 'I believe them with my heart. In my gut'; and Neo's narrated reaction to his intensity.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is the sixth and the last, the One — and that Neo will 'one day feel what I felt and know what I know.'
believes_about.wrong_because: This is the same certainty that already failed him five times; the scene seeds that his reading of prophecy is fallible and that his conviction may outrun what he can actually know about Neo.

believes_about.belief: That what Neo needs is not proof but trust, and that Neo's 'respect' for him can carry Neo across the door.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo agrees out of the emotional pull of Morpheus's zeal, not out of belief — so Morpheus may be mistaking Neo's surrender to intensity for the beginnings of genuine faith.

minds.wants: To stop being dragged toward a fate he doesn't want and to find some honest footing — either an exit from the pressure or a reason he can actually accept.
minds.feels: Cornered and disoriented: his entire prior reality has collapsed ('My entire life was a lie. I don't believe in anything anymore'), leaving him with nothing to argue from, which is precisely why Morpheus's certainty becomes the only thing to hold onto.
minds.shows: Resistance and sarcasm ('Are you kidding me?'), physical recoil from the handle, then a flat, exhausted capitulation — 'All right.'
minds.basis: Neo backing away from the spherical handle; his 'what's the point?' given he won't believe; his insistence that the prophecy 'sounds insane'; and the narrated 'rush from Morpheus's intensity' immediately before he agrees.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is a dangerous true-believer whose certainty is either madness or manipulation — a man who already got five others killed.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus's confession of having been 'terribly wrong' and humbled by those failures is genuine self-exposure, not zealot's blindness; Neo reads the intensity as fanaticism and misses the disciplined faith underneath it.

believes_about.belief: That agreeing to 'trust' is just giving in to pressure, a hollow 'All right' with no belief behind it.
believes_about.wrong_because: The 'rush' he feels is the first involuntary opening toward belief — he is further along than he admits, and this capitulation is the actual beginning of the faith he claims he'll never have.

minds.wants: To receive Neo at the threshold exactly as foreseen — she is a functionary of the Oracle's design, not a participant in the struggle.
minds.feels: Nothing legible as inner conflict; she is calm, prepared, and unsurprised, arriving the instant the handle turns.
minds.shows: A serene, timed greeting — 'Hello, Neo. You're right on time.'
minds.basis: The door opens on its own before Neo touches it and she addresses him by name as if his arrival were pre-scheduled.

connects_back: sc-082's elevator exchange about the Oracle as a 'guide' who is 'never wrong,' which sets up Neo's skepticism and the five-dead-candidates challenge.
sc-081/sc-082's physical descent (building, elevator) into the sealed, inevitable space where the threshold confrontation occurs.
The prior establishment of Morpheus as the man who was told he would 'find the One,' now tested against his own history of error.
sets_up: ev-021: Neo crossing the Oracle's threshold and submitting to her test of perception.
ev-021: The Oracle's prophecy, which only works if Neo has surrendered enough trust to be tested at all.
ev-026: Neo's later willingness to insist he can bring Morpheus back — the first seed of Neo trusting his own conviction over reason.
dramatic_function: To convert the abstract prophecy into an interpersonal crisis of faith, forcing Morpheus to risk his credibility by confessing past failure so that Neo's capitulation becomes a genuine, if reluctant, act of trust rather than a reasoned agreement — the hinge that lets the Oracle's test proceed.
